To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the slopes of regression lines are mostly linear or curved, positive and in magnitude depend on the types of CH and CC bond distances and angles.
the GIAO HF/6-311G * calculations of 1 H and C chemical shifts are in good agreement with experimental data.

the influence of variations of CH and of CC bond lengths and of angles on 13 C and 1 H N M R chemical shifts is linear or slightly curved, positive and in magnitude strongly dependent on the kind of bonds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of systematic variations of molecular geometries on calculated chemical shifts of 1 H and of 13 C nuclei.
the systematic investigation of the influence of variations of geometric parameters on ab initio calculated 1 H and/or 13 C chemical shifts.
the influence of systematic variations of molecular geometries on calculated 1H and13C NMR chemical shifts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GIAO HF/6-311G * calculations are suitable to predict 1 H and especially 13 C NNR chemical shifts in the range of 1-20 ppm with high accuracy.
the GIAO HF method is able to reproduce the influence of geometrical variations of the molecules on the 1 H and C NMR chemical shieldings with high reliability.
the calculated chemical shifts are very sensitive to variations of bond lengths but only to a small extent to bond angle variations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the systematic study of GIAO HF calculated chemical shifts with respect to systematic changes of bond lengths, bond angles and dihedral angles may be a powerful tool to understand the influence of these parameters on chemical shifts.
the calculated NMR chemical shifts of 1 H and of 13 C are dependent on the geometry and that these dependences can be used for a better understanding of chemical shifts.
the GIAO HF method is a reliable tool to study small variations of molecular geometries on chemical shifts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the GIAO method with the HF/6-311G** level of theory is a good choice for the calculation of 1 H and C NMR chemical shift values for small molecules, but it is important to use a large basis set and to take account of the effect of the solvent.
the influence of molecular geometries on calculated NMR shifts is not as large as it is sometimes believed.
the chemical shift values of the 1H and C-13 nuclei are very sensitive to the bond length variations.
